topics.label: LEADER selection threshold and processing
topics.description: The February 2026 order requires at least 60 points out of a maximum 100 for an operation to be selected. Local groups specify applicable criteria, points and minimums in their validated proposals. Passing this scoring gate does not establish applicant admissibility, eligible costs, a budget reservation or an award. The same order describes a non-competitive procedure, with applications instructed in registration order while budget is available. The GDR’s technical/managerial assessment and proposal are followed by the Delegación Territorial’s mandatory binding final admissibility/subsidisability report. These are documentary rules for this edition, with current applicability unverified.

source_refs.label: Processing: registration order, GDR review and final verification

topics.label: LEADER aid rates, caps and cofinancing
topics.description: Article 12 distinguishes reimbursement of actually incurred/paid eligible costs from fixed lump-sum aid. Typology-specific rules apply, subject to ceilings of 100% for non-productive and 65% for productive operations. For Lines 1–3, the order gives a general maximum of EUR 200,000 per operation, or EUR 400,000 for integral operations, without removing applicable minimis or typology conditions. These ceilings are not promised awards. The April call’s 85% FEADER/15% Andalusian split describes public programme financing, not an applicant’s aid intensity or own contribution. Budgets, other finance and eligible expenditure require separate checks.

topics.label: LEADER non-GDR call (April 2026 snapshot)
topics.description: The resolution dated 13 April and published 22 April 2026 calls Andalusian LEADER 7119.2 aid for applicants other than GDRs, procedure 25647. Applicants must match the beneficiary class of the applicable operation typology; natural persons must be self-employed or commit to that status within three months of a favourable award notification. Its stated application window runs from the day after publication of the required extract to 31 December 2028. That wording does not verify an opening date, current availability or remaining funds. Strategy/proposal modifications can suspend admissions during processing and change the applicable version; older initiated procedures retain their earlier basis. The call refers to detailed local criteria and annexes, so the library’s February AL20 tables are not automatically certified as the latest applicable version.

topics.label: LEADER criterion evidence and verification
topics.description: The September 2026 guide, version 2/public version 4, explains how selected LEADER criteria are checked. CadmSA means administrative control of the aid application; CadmSP concerns the payment application. Evidence must match the particular criterion and applicable local strategy. CO.1 requires identifying the operation’s objectives and the prioritized EDLL need, with final territorial verification. IN.1 requires a justified report from the instructing GDR against the latest applicable strategy. PT.1 distinguishes application evidence from proof of actual delivery, including project, completion/acceptance and photographs where relevant. Annex VII distinguishes mutually exclusive from cumulative subcriteria within each criterion; local family caps still matter. This guide is not a complete project score or a replacement for the locally selected rules.

topics.label: AL20 NPL1: water-cycle and consumption management
topics.description: NPL1 is the first LEADER-addressable need in the reviewed strategy: improving management of the water cycle and control of consumption, with a prioritization value of 3.28. That value is an output of the strategy’s priority exercise, not grant-selection points. A project would need to explain the actual need addressed and provide the criterion’s required evidence; buying a reservoir or drone does not itself satisfy CO.1. The library edition is a strategy snapshot whose later modifications and currently applicable local rules remain unverified.

topics.label: AL20 NPL4: soil regeneration, erosion and aridity
topics.description: NPL4 in the reviewed AL20 strategy calls for actions regenerating soils and reducing erosion and aridity, with a priority value of 3.16. It sits alongside NPL2 sustainable agriculture and NPL3 rural natural/cultural heritage. These are distinct strategic needs; their prioritization values do not award application points. The same strategy separately classifies broader natural-environment management measures under non-LEADER-addressable NPNL4. A restoration proposal therefore needs a justified mapping to the correct need, activity, applicant and funding rules rather than a blanket assumption that environmental work is eligible.

topics.label: AL20 innovation: technological precision agriculture
topics.description: Section 4.4 identifies technological precision agriculture, explicitly including drones and sensors, as integrated innovation aspect 11. Its justification focuses on municipalities with low agricultural production. Dalías and Berja are exceptions: there the text only envisages traditional, little-technified agriculture. This strategy example does not mean every drone use, ecological planting or reservoir-refill concept earns innovation points. The applicable operation, agricultural context, local version and GDR justification must be established. The source describes an innovation framing, not an evaluated drone-irrigation result or aviation permission.

topics.label: Prioritized local-strategy needs
topics.description: Source criterion CO.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. CO.1.1: one prioritized EDLL need (10 points); CO.1.2: two (12); CO.1.3: three or more (15). Starred needs depend on the strategy. The September guide marks CO.1.1–3 as mutually exclusive: the 10/12/15 tiers are alternatives, not a cumulative 37 points. Its application evidence must identify the operation and specific prioritized need; the final DT report confirms the fit. The reviewed strategy supplies NPL1 water management, NPL4 soil regeneration and other priorities, but this is not a project score.

topics.label: Local-strategy innovation
topics.description: Source criterion IN.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. IN.1.1: sector considered innovative in EDLL (0.02 points); IN.1.2: innovative theme (2.49); IN.1.3: innovative aspect (2.49). Family maximum 5. All refer to starred strategy definitions. The reviewed EDLL does not define a list of innovative sectors: it chooses themes and integrated aspects instead. Aspect 11 includes technological precision agriculture with drones/sensors under its stated municipal limits. The September guide marks IN.1 subcriteria cumulative but requires a GDR justification using the latest applicable strategy. Merely naming a new technology does not earn points.

topics.label: Positive action for rural youth
topics.description: Source criterion JR.3 for non-productive Line 3 operations. JR.3.1: courses for youth skills/employability (4 points); JR.3.2: dual vocational education or official youth placements (4); JR.3.3: return of recently qualified young people within 12 months of completing medium/higher education and labour-market incorporation in the zone (3); JR.3.4: awareness/training on youth contribution to local development (2); JR.3.5: rural youth leisure (4); JR.3.6: associations/participation and quality of life (4). Family maximum 4. Complete continuation: JR.3.7 creation/promotion of diversifying businesses providing products/services for young people (4 points); JR.3.8 response to one or more youth needs identified in EDL (2). Family maximum remains 4. In Annex VII of the September guide, JR.3.1/.2/.5/.6/.7 are exclusive; .3/.4/.8 are cumulative within the criterion. No project points are calculated.

topics.label: Enhancement of rural heritage
topics.description: Source criterion PT.1 for non-productive Line 3 operations. PT.1.1: natural/monumental/architectural/artistic heritage enhanced for subsequent use through physical work, training, dissemination or awareness (13 points); PT.1.2: traditional trades/gastronomic specialties identified in EDLL (7); PT.1.3: other heritage action identified as of interest in EDLL (2). Family maximum 15. The September verification guide distinguishes proof at application from actual implementation at payment. PT.1.1 investments use a basic project for the intended heritage use; payment evidence can include execution project, final works certificate, reception record and photographs. For strategy-dependent .2/.3, the guide requires GDR justification and the latest applicable EDL. Annex VII marks PT.1 subcriteria cumulative, subject to the AL20 family maximum of 15.

findings.label: Strategy priority values differ from project-selection points
findings.text: The strategy’s prioritization exercise weights mean general-priority responses at 85%, plus the relative frequency of links to climate, women and youth objectives at 5% each. NPL1 has 3.28; NPL2 sustainable agriculture 3.23; NPL3 rural heritage 3.22; NPL4 soils/erosion/aridity 3.16; NPL8 climate adaptation 3.12. These numbers rank needs within the strategy. CO.1 later awards alternative 10/12/15 application points for addressing 1/2/3-or-more justified prioritized needs; the two scales must not be combined.

source_refs.label: Prioritized needs and their strategy values

findings.label: Carbon-income innovation is not a LEADER funding entitlement
findings.text: The strategy places local initiatives earning income from carbon sinks under non-LEADER-addressable NPNL10 (priority value 2.56), while integrated innovation aspect 3 describes operations demonstrating carbon-sink income as one revenue source. These statements serve different strategy functions and do not establish that carbon-income generation itself is an eligible activity. Aspect 8 separately concerns certified efficient carbon/water footprints communicated to customers. The operation’s funding typology, evidence and current strategy must still be checked.

findings.label: Call finance is distinct from AL20 allocation and applicant aid
findings.text: The April call gives an overall EUR 97,589,590.75 allocation, divided into EUR 70,589,590.75 for 2026 and EUR 27,000,000 for 2027, with public cofinancing 85% FEADER and 15% Andalucía. The separately signed February AL20 activity/budget sheet lists Line 1 EUR 330,052.59, Line 2 EUR 989,725.78 and Line 3 EUR 710,649.89, totaling EUR 2,030,428.26. These are document-stated programme/line allocations, not remaining funds or an individual grant cap. The applicable later local proposal and balance have not been verified.

unresolved.text: The reviewed EDLL has no verified publication date, and the call permits later local strategy/proposal changes with admissions suspension. The February AL20 tables, April call and September guide are related documentary editions, but their current simultaneous applicability and remaining balances are unverified in library-only mode. Do not score a project until the full applicable set and project inputs are established.

The February AL20 AT.3 table uses INE 2023 and a municipal median. The September guide text refers to latest published data and median or mean, with 2,497 as Andalusian reference; its Annex VII still mentions INE 2023. Preserve these documentary differences. The actual applicable data series, local statistic and settlement must be confirmed before awarding population points.

browse_groups.description: Start with the three local activity lines, then distinguish selection, aid ceilings and the dated call. The order requires at least 60/100 and the procedure also depends on admissibility, budget and the applicable local version.
